- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.67+), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price drops, model underreacts; add 1–3% upward bias for next 3–5 days to avoid underestimating rebound.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, model often misses the bottom; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows 2+ consecutive high values (≥0.67), model tends to overforecast; apply 3–5% downward correction for next 5 days.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 3 days, model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent 3-day average for next 5 days.
